title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.651). S = Spec A is integral with generic point y, K = k(y) of characteristic 0, and G is a group scheme over S. A homomorphism phi_y : G_{a,K} -> G_K is given, with g = phi_y(1) extending to a section of G over S. The question is whether phi_y extends to a homomorphism f : G_{a,S} -> G.

On this page Grothendieck tests the question on G = GL(M) = Aut(M), with M free of rank n over A. Since char K = 0, phi_y(lambda) = exp(lambda X) = sum_i X^i lambda^i / i!, where X is in End_A(M) tensor K and X^n = 0 (eq. 8). The hypothesis that g and g^{-1} are integral reads: exp(X) and exp(-X) lie in End_A(M) (eq. 9). Since phi_y is a polynomial in lambda, it extends to G_{a,S} -> GL(M) exactly when every coefficient is integral: X^i/i! in End_A(M) for 1 <= i <= n-1 (eq. 10). This is a correct reduction.

He declares n=2 trivial and treats n=3 (after a crossed-out attempt) as having only one denominator. He then writes n=4: phi(lambda) = 1 + X lambda + X^2/2 lambda^2 + X^3/6 lambda^3. From phi(1), phi(-1) in M_4(A) he deduces (11): X^2/2 +/- X^3/6 in M_4(A). He asks whether (12) follows: X^2/2 and X^3/6 in M_4(A). He says this is clear if 2 is invertible, since then X^2 and hence X^3/6 are integral. He locates the difficulty in residue characteristic 2. The next page sets X = X_0/2^nu with A a DVR of uniformizer 2, and then retreats to proving a 'Théorème' on generically unipotent sections.

What the page is circling is a model-theoretic question. The schematic closure L of the generic one-parameter subgroup {u^lambda} in GL_{n,A} need not be G_{a,A}. For u = 1+N, its coordinate ring is A[binom(lambda,i), i<n] (a 'binomial' or integer-valued-polynomial model of G_a). Its special fiber can have non-neutral components; this is exactly the worry on the previous page about L^0 and non-neutral components of L_s.
errors: (11) silently assumes X is in M_4(A). From exp(X) and exp(-X) integral one only gets exp(X)+exp(-X) = 2 + X^2 and exp(X)-exp(-X) = 2X + X^3/3 integral; integrality of X itself is not given. The next page then lets X be non-integral, X = X_0/2^nu, which is inconsistent with (11).

The claim that n=3 is trivial is false when 2 is not a unit (the word 'aussi' is crossed out, suggesting hesitation). Counterexample over A = Z_2, n=3: N is the 3x3 Jordan nilpotent and X = log(1+N) = N - N^2/2. Then exp(+/-X) = (1+N)^{+/-1} are integral, but X and X^2/2 = N^2/2 are not. Here (1+N)^lambda = 1 + lambda N + lambda(lambda-1)/2 N^2 does not have A-integral coefficients in lambda.

'Si 2 inv. dans A c'est clair' is also wrong, because of the hidden assumption that X is integral. Over A = Z_3 with n=4, take X = log(1+N) = N - N^2/2 + N^3/3: exp(+/-X) is integral but X and X^3/6 are not. So the answer to question (12), in the setting (9)->(10), is negative in general.

The correct statement: if the residue characteristic is p and X^p = 0 (i.e. n <= p), then log(u) = sum_{i<p} (-1)^{i+1}(u-1)^i/i is integral and all X^i/i! (i < p) are integral, so phi_y extends. In general (n > p) it fails, already for regular unipotent u in GL_n over Z_p.
Hence the obstruction is not specific to residue characteristic 2. It arises for every residue characteristic p < n.

ideas.what: Reduction of extending the generic one-parameter subgroup exp(lambda X) over S to integrality of the divided powers X^i/i! (in GL_n)
ideas.modern_name: Integrality of the exponential / divided-power (binomial) models of G_a; extension of homomorphisms over a DVR
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Serre and Seitz for exponentiation of unipotent elements when p >= nilpotency order
ideas.where_published: Related material on extending group homomorphisms over a base is in SGA3, but this specific computation is not known to be there

ideas.what: Question: does integrality of g = exp(X) and g^{-1} force integrality of X^i/i!, i.e. does every generically unipotent integral section lie on an integral G_a?
ideas.modern_name: Exponentiation of unipotent elements in mixed characteristic; saturation; 'good' A1-subgroups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (saturation, 1990s); Seitz (2000, unipotent elements and saturation); Balaji–Deligne–Parameswaran (2017, complete reducibility and saturation over DVRs)

ideas.what: Schematic closure of a generic G_a in G may have special fiber with non-neutral components and non-reduced identity component (via (1+N)^lambda with binomial coefficients)
ideas.modern_name: Non-standard integral models of G_a (dilatations, binomial-polynomial models)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Waterhouse–Weisfeiler; Raynaud (dilatations); work on models of G_a over DVRs

missed.claim: Grothendieck leaves open (and on the next page seeks a counterexample or theorem for) whether integral exp(+/-X) forces integral X^i/i!. The answer is negative via X = log(1+N) for a Jordan block with n > p, and positive when n <= p. This is consistent with later literature on exponentiation and saturation; nothing new beyond the archival record of his engagement.
missed.quote: on se demande s'il en résulte (12) X^2/2, X^3/6 ∈ M_4(A) ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck anticipating the p >= h type conditions for extending unipotent elements to G_a-subgroups over mixed-characteristic bases (Seitz, Balaji–Deligne–Parameswaran). Historically interesting but not mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: An exploratory computation about integrality of exponentials over a mixed-characteristic base. The question is natural and its answer (negative for n > p, positive for n <= p) is classical in later saturation/exponentiation literature. The page contains gaps (hidden integrality of X, a false 'n=3 trivial' claim), but no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'endomorphismes nilp. tens.[?]' is almost certainly 'endomorphismes nilpotents' of M_K.
In line 'Pour n=3 [-aussi-]' the crossed-out word appears to be 'aussi', i.e. Grothendieck retracted the claim that n=3 is trivial.
'jauge[?]' is uncertain from the image; it plausibly describes A (e.g. a DVR or 'trait'), but the reading cannot be confirmed.
